name: power_latch
summary: A push-on soft power latch for a battery board: a button press switches the cell through, the MCU holds it on, and the press is readable as a clean logic level
note: From simple_earring rev 2 (vendored with the bolt earring: boards/bolt-earring/vendor/simple_earring/scripts/circuit.py, whose comments give the reasons and the corner simulations behind each value). Q_SW, a P-FET, switches the cell to OUT when its gate (LATCH_G) is pulled low; R_GATE holds it off. Pressing the button pulls BTN low, which pulls LATCH_G low through one anode of D_OR, so the board comes on; the MCU then drives HOLD high and Q_HOLD keeps LATCH_G low after the button is released. R_HOLD keeps HOLD low until firmware drives it, so the latch is off at boot and while the MCU is in reset. D_OR's other anode pulls PRESS_N low on a press; Q_SENSE, a P-FET from VIO, turns that into PRESSED, high while the button is held (a P-FET because the diode's low, about 0.45 V, is too near a Schmitt input's threshold but is plenty of gate drive). R_SENSE pulls PRESSED low: the MCU pin's own pull-up must be off. C_DEB debounces the button (R_GATE x C_DEB, 10 ms, on release) and is the second ESD stage behind button_esd. Q_SW carries only what OUT feeds (an enable line and a divider in the bolt), so a weak part with a high threshold is chosen: leakage into LATCH_G with the board off must not reach its threshold, hot.

Q_HOLD.note: The MCU's hold: drain on LATCH_G

R_HOLD.note: HOLD low until firmware drives it: off at boot

D_OR.note: Two diodes, common cathode (3) on BTN: anode 2 on LATCH_G, anode 1 on PRESS_N

C_DEB.note: Debounce, and the second ESD stage

Q_SENSE.note: P-channel inverter: source VIO, drain PRESSED

OUT.note: The cell while the latch is on: an enable line and light loads, not the system current

BTN.note: The button's node: pulled low (through button_esd) to press

PRESSED.note: High while the button is held

citations.figure: SC70(SOT-323) outline with pins 1, 2 and 3, and the P-channel symbol labelled 1 Gate, 2 Source, 3 Drain.
citations.note: Q_SW. KiCad's BSS84 symbol (extends TP0610T) is G 1, S 2, D 3.

Gate Threshold Voltage VGS(th), min / typ / max in volts. The 0.8 V minimum is what board-off leakage into LATCH_G through R_GATE must stay under; pressed, LATCH_G sits a diode drop above ground (~0.5-0.7 V), so VGS is about -2.3 V at a 3.0 V cell, past the -2 V maximum. No temperature coefficient is given.
Q_HOLD. Table-2; KiCad's BSS138 symbol (Q_NMOS_GSD) is G 1, S 2, D 3 as well.

citations.quote: Gate Threshold Voltage VGS(TH) VGS=VDS, ID=250uA 0.8 1.0 1.5 V
citations.note: HOLD's vih of 1.5 V is the maximum threshold.

citations.quote: 1 A1 anode (diode 1) 2 A2 anode (diode 2) 3 CC common cathode
citations.note: Table 2. KiCad's BAV70 symbol: A 1, A 2, K 3.

IR max per diode. With the board off PRESS_N is at 0 V and BTN near the cell, so D_OR's PRESS_N diode is reverse-biased and its leakage flows through R_GATE: part of the LATCH_G budget. Hot it is far larger: the next row is 30 uA max at 25 V, Tj 150 °C.
VF max at 1 mA: on a press LATCH_G and PRESS_N sit one diode drop above BTN, and the currents here (R_GATE's and R_PRESS's tens of uA) are well under 1 mA.
Q_SENSE; matches KiCad's BSS84 symbol (G 1, S 2, D 3).

citations.quote: Gate-Source Threshold Voltage VGS(th) VDS =VGS, ID =-250µA -0.45 -0.7 V
citations.note: Min and typ only: the datasheet gives no maximum. Q_SENSE's gate is driven to PRESS_N's diode low, about VIO - 0.45 V of VGS.
RDS(on) max in mOhm at VGS -1.8 V: the part is specified fully on at a VGS well inside the ~2.85 V Q_SENSE gets from a 3.3 V VIO, which stands in for the missing VGS(th) maximum.
The bolt's button (button_esd's B3U-3000P): C_DEB's 10 ms release time constant (R_GATE x C_DEB) is longer than the bounce.
